source.original_text:
Let $X_t$ be a jointly measurable unit-sphere-valued process with almost surely continuous paths. Suppose its actual coordinates satisfy the specified integrated Brownian equation at every positive finite horizon with projected noise and its radial drift. For each twice continuously differentiable ambient test, the derivative of its expectation is the expected spherical generator. This is the ordinary derivative at positive times and the right derivative at time zero.

The coordinate set is finite with decidable equality. The ambient measure is a probability measure. Standard vector Brownian motion is relative to the filtration, which satisfies the usual conditions.
The sphere-valued process is jointly measurable and its paths are almost surely continuous. The field $u(t,w)$ is jointly continuous and takes ambient vector values. The deterministic temperature is continuous and nonnegative.
At each positive horizon, the integrated rows use initial coordinates strongly measurable for the time-zero filtration σ-algebra, strongly progressive drift with almost surely integrable time sections, and progressive product-square-integrable Brownian integrands. The Euclidean representation agrees with the supplied sphere process at all times in that horizon almost surely.
Almost surely throughout each horizon, the drift is $-u(t,X_t)-\lambda_t(d-1)X_t$ and the $j$th noise column is $\sqrt{2\lambda_t}(e_j-(X_t)_jX_t)$. The test is $C^2$ at every sphere point.

\frac{d}{dt}\mathbb E[f(X_t)]=\mathbb E[-Df(X_t)[u(t,X_t)]+\lambda_t\Delta_{S^{d-1}}^{\rm ext}f(X_t)].

blind_reconstruction.text:
Let I be finite with decidable equality, Omega measurable, P a probability measure, F a filtration satisfying the usual conditions for mu=P, and B an R^I-valued standard Brownian motion with F. A vector standard Brownian motion with filtration F here starts at zero for every sample, has jointly independent increments over each finite family of disjoint half-open intervals, has centered Gaussian increment projections with variance (t-s)*||ell||^2 for every continuous linear functional ell and s<t, has almost surely continuous paths, is strongly F-adapted, and has each increment from s to t independent of F_s when s<=t. Usual conditions mean every null subset of Omega belongs to every F_t, and F is right-continuous. Write lambda_H for real Lebesgue measure restricted to [0,H] and transported to NNReal. A progressive L2 integrand on horizon H is a real strongly F-progressive process belonging to L2(mu product lambda_H), after ordering its arguments as (omega,t). Write I^H_j(h)(t) for its specified completed Ito integral against the coordinate B_j(t,omega) of B. This is the canonical elementary-approximation path limit, patched to zero on its exceptional null set and held constant after H. Put S={w in EuclideanSpace R I: ||w||=1}, d=card(I), k=real(d-1 in Nat), p_j(w)=e_j-w_j*w, and Lf(w)=Laplacian(f)(w)-D(Df)(w)[w][w]-k*Df(w)[w]. Thus the subtraction in k is natural-number subtraction before casting. Sphere values carry their induced topology and Borel structure and are included in the ambient Euclidean space in derivative formulas. Let X:[0,infinity) x Omega->S be jointly measurable with globally continuous time paths for P-almost every omega. Let u:[0,infinity) x S->R^I be jointly continuous and a:[0,infinity)->R continuous and pointwise nonnegative. Assume the following horizon-by-horizon representation: for every H>0 there exist eta_ij (i,j in I), each a progressive L2 integrand on [0,H], x:Omega->R^I with every coordinate strongly F_0-measurable, and b_i:[0,infinity) x Omega->R with every b_i strongly F-progressive and, for each i, b_i(.,omega) integrable on [0,H] for almost every omega. They satisfy, for almost every omega and all t<=H, the vector identity
X(t,omega)=(x_i(omega)+integral_{[0,t]} b_i(v,omega)dv+sum_j I^H_j(eta_ij)(t,omega))_{i in I}.
They also satisfy, for almost every omega and all t<=H, (b_i(t,omega))_i=-u(t,X(t,omega))-a(t)*k*X(t,omega), and, for almost every omega, all t<=H and all j, (eta_ij(t,omega))_i=sqrt(2*a(t))*p_j(X(t,omega)). These a.e. assertions are separate conjuncts. For every f:R^I->R that is C2 at each point of S and every s>=0, the real function r mapped to integral_Omega f(X(r^+,omega))dP has derivative within [0,infinity) at s equal to integral_Omega [-Df(X(s,omega))[u(s,X(s,omega))]+a(s)*Lf(X(s,omega))]dP, with r^+=max(r,0). At s=0 this is a right derivative; at s>0 it is the usual derivative. Strong progressiveness of X itself is not a separate hypothesis.

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.SphereWeakForward

open Filter MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory Set
open scoped BigOperators NNReal
open BrownianMotion ProgressiveL2 EuclideanBrownianCoordinates ItoIntegralProcess
  ProgressiveDriftIntegral SphereItoFormula TimeMeasureRealBridge WeakMartingaleEvolution
open AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Geometry.SphereProjectedNoise
  AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Geometry.SphereDiffusionGenerator

/-- A sphere-valued process with the specified integrated Brownian equations
on each positive horizon satisfies the weak forward equation for smooth tests. -/
theorem hasDerivWithinAt_sphere_expectation_of_ito_rows
    {Ω I : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]
    {filtration : Filtration ℝ≥0 (inferInstance : MeasurableSpace Ω)}
    (P : ProbabilityMeasure Ω) {B : ℝ≥0 → Ω → EuclideanSpace ℝ I}
    (hB : IsStandardBrownianMotionWithFiltration B filtration (P : Measure Ω))
    (hUsual : SatisfiesUsualConditions filtration (P : Measure Ω))
    (X : ℝ≥0 → Ω → Metric.sphere (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ I) 1)
    (hX : Measurable (Function.uncurry X))
    (hPaths : ∀ᵐ ω ∂(P : Measure Ω), Continuous (fun t => X t ω))
    (u : ℝ≥0 → Metric.sphere (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ I) 1 → EuclideanSpace ℝ I)
    (hu : Continuous (Function.uncurry u))
    (temperature : ℝ≥0 → ℝ) (hTemperature : Continuous temperature)
    (hNonneg : ∀ t, 0 ≤ temperature t)
    (hEquation : ∀ (T : ℝ≥0) (hT : 0 < T),
      ∃ (η : I → I → ProgressiveL2Integrand filtration (P : Measure Ω) T)
        (x : Ω → I → ℝ) (b : I → ℝ≥0 → Ω → ℝ),
        (∀ i, StronglyMeasurable[filtration 0] (fun ω => x ω i)) ∧
        (∀ i, IsStronglyProgressive filtration (b i)) ∧
        (∀ i, ∀ᵐ ω ∂(P : Measure Ω), Integrable (fun t => b i t ω) (TimeMeasure.upTo T)) ∧
        (∀ᵐ ω ∂(P : Measure Ω), ∀ t ≤ T,
          (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i : I => x ω i + prefixIntegralProcess (b i) t ω +
            ∑ j : I, itoIntegralProcess (η i j) hT ((coordinateFamily hB).isBrownian j) hUsual t ω) :
              EuclideanSpace ℝ I) = (X t ω : EuclideanSpace ℝ I)) ∧
        (∀ᵐ ω ∂(P : Measure Ω), ∀ t ≤ T, WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => b i t ω) =
          -u t (X t ω) - (temperature t * ((Fintype.card I - 1 : ℕ) : ℝ)) •
            (X t ω : EuclideanSpace ℝ I)) ∧
        (∀ᵐ ω ∂(P : Measure Ω), ∀ t ≤ T, ∀ j : I, WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (η i j).process t ω) =
          Real.sqrt (2 * temperature t) • projectedNoiseColumn j (X t ω)))
    (f : EuclideanSpace ℝ I → ℝ)
    (hf : ∀ w ∈ Metric.sphere (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ I) 1, ContDiffAt ℝ 2 f w)
    (s : ℝ≥0) :
    HasDerivWithinAt (fun t : ℝ => ∫ ω, f (X t.toNNReal ω) ∂(P : Measure Ω))
      (∫ ω, -fderiv ℝ f (X s ω) (u s (X s ω)) + temperature s * sphereLaplacian f (X s ω)
        ∂(P : Measure Ω)) (Ici 0) (s : ℝ) := by
  obtain ⟨ω₀⟩ := nonempty_of_isProbabilityMeasure (P : Measure Ω)
  let E := EuclideanSpace ℝ I
  let S := Metric.sphere (0 : E) 1
  have : CompactSpace S := isCompact_iff_compactSpace.mp (isCompact_sphere _ _)
  let A (t : ℝ≥0) (w : S) : ℝ :=
    -fderiv ℝ f w (u t w) + temperature t * sphereLaplacian f w
  have hg : Continuous (fun w : S => f (w : E)) := continuous_iff_continuousAt.2 fun w =>
    (hf w w.property).continuousAt.comp continuous_subtype_val.continuousAt
  have hD : Continuous (fun w : S => fderiv ℝ f (w : E)) :=
    continuous_iff_continuousAt.2 fun w =>
      ((hf w w.property).continuousAt_fderiv (by decide)).comp continuous_subtype_val.continuousAt
  have hH : Continuous (fun w : S => fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) (w : E)) :=
    continuous_iff_continuousAt.2 fun w =>
      (((hf w w.property).fderiv_right (m := 1) (by decide)).continuousAt_fderiv
        (by decide)).comp continuous_subtype_val.continuousAt
  have hTrace : Continuous (fun w : S => ∑ j : I,
      fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) (w : E) (projectedNoiseColumn j w) (projectedNoiseColumn j w)) := by
    apply continuous_finsetSum
    intro j _
    let L : E →L[ℝ] ℝ := PiLp.proj (p := 2) (𝕜 := ℝ) (β := fun _ : I => ℝ) j
    have hp : Continuous (fun w : S => projectedNoiseColumn j (w : E)) :=
      continuous_const.sub ((L.continuous.comp continuous_subtype_val).smul continuous_subtype_val)
    exact (hH.clm_apply hp).clm_apply hp
  have hLap : Continuous (fun w : S => sphereLaplacian f (w : E)) := by
    refine (hTrace.sub ((continuous_const (y := ((Fintype.card I - 1 : ℕ) : ℝ))).mul
      (hD.clm_apply continuous_subtype_val))).congr ?_
    intro w
    change (∑ j : I, fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) (w : E)
      (projectedNoiseColumn j w) (projectedNoiseColumn j w)) -
      ((Fintype.card I - 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) * fderiv ℝ f (w : E) (w : E) = _
    rw [sum_hessian_projectedNoiseColumn f (mem_sphere_zero_iff_norm.1 w.property)]
    rfl
  have hA : Continuous (Function.uncurry A) :=
    ((hD.comp continuous_snd).clm_apply hu).neg.add
      ((hTemperature.comp continuous_fst).mul (hLap.comp continuous_snd))
  apply hasDerivWithinAt_expectation_of_centered_balance P X hX hPaths
    (fun w : S => f (w : E)) hg A hA
  intro T
  by_cases hT : T = 0
  · subst T
    exact ⟨0, integrable_zero Ω ℝ _, integral_zero _ _,
      Eventually.of_forall fun _ => by simp⟩
  have hPos : 0 < T := bot_lt_iff_ne_bot.mpr hT
  obtain ⟨η, x, b, hx, hb, hbi, hEq, hbEq, hηEq⟩ := hEquation T hPos
  let Y (t : ℝ≥0) (ω : Ω) : E := WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i : I =>
    x ω i + prefixIntegralProcess (b i) t ω +
      ∑ j : I, itoIntegralProcess (η i j) hPos ((coordinateFamily hB).isBrownian j) hUsual t ω)
  have hYEq : ∀ᵐ ω ∂(P : Measure Ω), ∀ t ≤ T, Y t ω = (X t ω : E) := hEq
  have hSphere : ∀ᵐ ω ∂(P : Measure Ω), ∀ t ≤ T, Y t ω ∈ S :=
    hYEq.mono fun ω heq t ht => (heq t ht).symm ▸ (X t ω).property
  have hU : ∀ᵐ ω ∂(P : Measure Ω), ContinuousOn (fun t => u t (X t ω)) (Icc 0 T) :=
    hPaths.mono fun _ hω => (hu.comp (continuous_id.prodMk hω)).continuousOn
  have hDrift : ∀ᵐ ω ∂(P : Measure Ω), ∀ t ≤ T, WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => b i t ω) =
      -u t (X t ω) - (temperature t * ((Fintype.card I - 1 : ℕ) : ℝ)) • Y t ω := by
    filter_upwards [hYEq, hbEq] with ω heq hcoeff t ht
    rw [heq t ht]
    exact hcoeff t ht
  have hColumns : ∀ᵐ ω ∂(P : Measure Ω), ∀ t ≤ T, ∀ j : I,
      WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (η i j).process t ω) =
      Real.sqrt (2 * temperature t) • projectedNoiseColumn j (Y t ω) := by
    filter_upwards [hYEq, hηEq] with ω heq hcoeff t ht j
    rw [heq t ht]
    exact hcoeff t ht j
  obtain ⟨M, hM, hM0, hIto⟩ := ito_formula_sphere_at_horizon hB hPos hUsual η x hx b hb hbi
    (X 0 ω₀) f hf (fun t ω => u t (X t ω)) hU temperature hTemperature.continuousOn
    (fun t _ => hNonneg t) hSphere hDrift hColumns
  have hmean := hM.setIntegral_eq (show 0 ≤ T from bot_le) MeasurableSet.univ
  rw [Measure.restrict_univ] at hmean
  simp only [hM0, integral_zero] at hmean
  refine ⟨M T, hM.integrable T, hmean.symm, ?_⟩
  filter_upwards [hYEq, hIto] with ω heq hω
  change f (Y T ω) - f (Y 0 ω) =
    (∫ t, -fderiv ℝ f (Y t ω) (u t (X t ω)) + temperature t * sphereLaplacian f (Y t ω)
      ∂(TimeMeasure.upTo T)) + M T ω at hω
  rw [heq T le_rfl, heq 0 bot_le] at hω
  rw [hω]
  apply congrArg (· + M T ω)
  calc
    _ = ∫ t, A t (X t ω) ∂(TimeMeasure.upTo T) := by
      apply integral_congr_ae
      filter_upwards [TimeMeasure.ae_mem_Ioc_zero_upTo T] with t ht
      simp only [heq t ht.2, A]
    _ = _ := by
      rw [← TimeMeasure.restrict_upTo_Ioc_zero T,
        integral_upTo_restrict_Ioc_eq_real (fun t => A t (X t ω)) (show 0 ≤ T from bot_le) le_rfl]
      apply intervalIntegral.integral_congr
      intro r hr
      change r ∈ uIcc (0 : ℝ) (T : ℝ) at hr
      rw [uIcc_of_le T.coe_nonneg] at hr
      simp only [realZeroExtension, if_pos hr.1]

end AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.SphereWeakForward

steps.title: Obtain a centered increment on each horizon
steps.text: On each positive horizon, the integrated Euclidean rows agree with the supplied sphere process throughout the horizon on a common full-measure event. Transfer the terminal Itô identity along this agreement. Its zero-start martingale has an integrable terminal value with mean zero. At horizon zero take the residual to be zero.

steps.title: Put the balance on the real time axis
steps.text: The horizon measure agrees with ordinary Lebesgue time after embedding the nonnegative interval into the reals. The sphere generator is jointly continuous because the test derivatives are continuous along the sphere and the projected trace is a finite sum.

      apply integral_congr_ae

      simp only [heq t ht.2, A]
    _ = _ := by
      rw [← TimeMeasure.restrict_upTo_Ioc_zero T,

steps.text: Apply the centered-residual derivative theorem to the same sphere process at all horizons.

lesson.lean_statement: The theorem concludes a derivative within the nonnegative real half-line, including its right derivative at zero. The integrated coordinate witnesses can be chosen separately at each positive horizon.
lesson.lean_proof: Build one centered terminal increment per horizon from the completed Itô martingale, then apply the compact-state expectation theorem.

candidate_assumptions.lean: The coordinate set is finite with decidable equality. The ambient measure is a probability measure. Standard vector Brownian motion is relative to the filtration, which satisfies the usual conditions.

candidate_assumptions.source: The sphere-valued process is jointly measurable and its paths are almost surely continuous. The field $u(t,w)$ is jointly continuous and takes ambient vector values. The deterministic temperature is continuous and nonnegative.
candidate_assumptions.lean: The sphere-valued process is jointly measurable and its paths are almost surely continuous. The field $u(t,w)$ is jointly continuous and takes ambient vector values. The deterministic temperature is continuous and nonnegative.

candidate_assumptions.source: At each positive horizon, the integrated rows use initial coordinates strongly measurable for the time-zero filtration σ-algebra, strongly progressive drift with almost surely integrable time sections, and progressive product-square-integrable Brownian integrands. The Euclidean representation agrees with the supplied sphere process at all times in that horizon almost surely.

candidate_assumptions.source: Almost surely throughout each horizon, the drift is $-u(t,X_t)-\lambda_t(d-1)X_t$ and the $j$th noise column is $\sqrt{2\lambda_t}(e_j-(X_t)_jX_t)$. The test is $C^2$ at every sphere point.
